Hi, I'm the Playwright bot and I took a first look.

**Reproduced on 1.64.1 and fixed on the current `@next` build.** With two CPUs, WebKit r2370 produced 0 fps for the 12 `backdrop-filter` cards, while r2359 produced 47 fps and r2376 produced 43 fps. This confirms a WebKit regression in the browser revision pinned by Playwright 1.64.x, not an application or test-runner issue.

#43084 introduced r2370, and the r2373 roll in #43191 is merged on `main`. Until a release includes the newer WebKit revision, the available workarounds are to stay on 1.63 or use `@next`.

<details>
<summary>What I ran</summary>

I ran the provided script headless in `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble`, constrained with `--cpuset-cpus=0,1`, using the iPhone 13 device settings:

| Playwright | WebKit revision | Filter off | Filter on |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1.63.0 | r2359 (WebKit 26.6) | 55 fps | 47 fps |
| 1.64.1 | r2370 (WebKit 27.2) | 55 fps | 0 fps |
| 1.65.0-alpha-2026-10-15 (`@next`) | r2376 (WebKit 27.2) | 55 fps | 43 fps |

The current checkout at `343d8e7d0f59` also pins r2376.
</details>


<sub>Triaged on Linux by the Playwright bot - [agent run](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/actions/runs/38778714900)</sub>
<!-- playwright-ai-triage -->

The fix in r2373 and later is only partial. The upstream cause is WebKit 322150@main. Since r2373, the problem is hidden only when the elements with `backdrop-filter` do not overlap. When they overlap, the paint time still doubles with each element on the current build (r2376). For example, 14 overlapping elements take more than 4 seconds per frame, even with a GPU.

Upstream report: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=327850

title: [Regression]: Linux WebKit r2370 (1.64.0, 1.64.1) renders pages with backdrop-filter at ~0 fps on 2 CPUs; fine in r2369 and r2373+
